I think gun collecting gives us a perspective that there isn't really any thing that' new. With the advent of the metallic cartridge in the American Civil war, (Oh I know that metallic cartridges pre-dates the civil war but the Spencer carbine was the first wide spread metallic cartridge rifle) and the modern Gatling guns found on aircraft and now on the ground differ very little from Dr. Richards Gatling wonderful gun of 1862. Well Dr. Gatling cheated a bit. The Gatling gun was an adaptation of his much earlier cotton and grain sowing machine. We call them grain drills today. The were a wheel driven cam operated plunger and barrel that allowed you to deposit a single grain seed obtained from a hopper, at a certain depth at a certain interval as it was towed behind a team of horses. The first gas and recoil operated weapons saw the light of day just before the turn of the century. In fact the notorious outlaw Frank James ( of the James gang) during the later years of his life carried a 1903 Colt .32 cal hamerless auto pistol. Can any one say recoil operated striker fired? Sig. Glock. FN, Walther. Kahr, and others, have come late to that party (About 110 years to late). So you can see why we gun collectors are a strange flock of birds, because we know there ain't nothing new no more.
